title: this and binding
learningObjectives: Explain this and binding and debug or organise JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: The value of this depends on how a function is called, except in arrow functions where this is lexical. Methods receive the object used as the call receiver; detached functions may lose that receiver. call(), apply(), and bind() can control this for ordinary functions.
understand.whyItMatters: Incorrect this assumptions cause bugs when methods are passed as callbacks or event handlers. Use arrow functions for lexical this where appropriate, or bind a method when its receiver must be preserved.
understand.analogy: this is the current call context for an ordinary function; the call site helps determine which object it refers to.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; debugger, module, prototype, and function-call behaviour follow JavaScript and browser runtime rules.

explain.narrative: Calling the method through learner supplies learner as this. call explicitly supplies the receiver for the detached function.

examples.explanation: Calling the method through learner supplies learner as this. call explicitly supplies the receiver for the detached function.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page demonstrates the code organisation or runtime behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Detach an object method and observe its this behaviour. Restore the receiver with bind or call and compare with an arrow function.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example that uses the feature. Inspect its runtime behaviour and explain the scope, receiver, or call path involved.
hints: Use breakpoints to inspect changing values.
Test methods both through their object and when passed as callbacks.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>this and binding</title></head><body>
<script>const learner={name:'Asha',greet(){return `Hello ${this.name}`;}};const detached=learner.greet;console.log(learner.greet());console.log(detached.call(learner));</script>
</body></html>
